facts.t: American judicial review is not in the American Constitution
facts.d: Article III says nothing about striking down laws. Chief Justice Marshall asserted the power in Marbury v. Madison (1803) and it has been accepted ever since — a doctrine as judge-made as India's basic structure.

facts.t: British courts cannot strike down an Act of Parliament
facts.d: Under the Human Rights Act 1998 the most they can issue is a declaration of incompatibility, which leaves the statute fully in force. Parliament then chooses whether to amend it — the dialogic model, as against India's supremacist one.

facts.t: India is the only one of the three that reviews amendments
facts.d: Once ratified under Article V, an American amendment is not substantively reviewable. Britain has no formal amendment process at all. India's basic structure doctrine makes constitutional amendments themselves justiciable — the strongest form of review anywhere.

bank.q: Judicial review in the United States was established by:
o: Article III of the Constitution expressly
bank.e: Marbury v. Madison. The Constitution does not confer the power in terms — it was asserted by the Court.

bank.q: Comparing the three systems, consider the following statements:
s: Indian courts can strike down constitutional amendments.
American courts can substantively review a ratified amendment.
British courts cannot strike down primary legislation.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Once ratified under Article V, an American amendment is not substantively reviewable.

bank.q: Match List I (jurisdiction) with List II (foundational case or source):
pairs: 1. CCSU v. Minister for the Civil Service
bank.e: Kesavananda for India, Marbury for the United States, CCSU for the common-law grounds of review, and the Human Rights Act 1998 as the statutory rights source.

bank.q: The three grounds of review laid down in the CCSU case are:
o: Ultra vires, mala fides and arbitrariness
bank.e: Illegality, irrationality and procedural impropriety — with proportionality later added as a fourth ground, particularly under the Human Rights Act.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a limit on judicial review in the United States?
bank.e: Parliamentary sovereignty is the defining British limit. The United States has constitutional supremacy, with justiciability doctrines instead.

bank.as: India's standing rules are the most liberal of the three systems.
bank.rs: Public interest litigation permits representative litigation on behalf of those unable to approach the court.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The United States requires concrete injury, causation and redressability; Britain applies a sufficient-interest test that is flexible but not PIL-oriented.

bank.q: With reference to remedies, consider the following statements:
s: India offers five writs, along with continuing mandamus and judicial guidelines.
The United Kingdom's Judicial Review and Courts Act 2022 introduced suspended quashing orders.
American courts routinely issue advisory opinions.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. American federal courts do not give advisory opinions — a long-standing limit flowing from the case-or-controversy requirement.

bank.q: Under the Scotland Act, legislation outside devolved competence is:
o: Voidable at the discretion of the court
bank.e: It is simply not law. Devolution is the one area where British courts exercise something close to constitutional review.

bank.q: All of the following describe the British model EXCEPT:
o: Dialogic, with Parliament retaining final authority
Rights protection weaker against Parliament than against public authorities
Constitutional supremacy enforced through a written charter
bank.e: The United Kingdom has an uncodified constitution and legally sovereign Parliament — the opposite of enforced constitutional supremacy.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about rights protection:
s: India applies substantive due process under Article 21 after Maneka Gandhi.
The United States applies tiers of scrutiny.
The United Kingdom permits courts to invalidate statutes that breach Convention rights.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. British courts may only interpret compatibly or declare incompatibility; the statute stands either way.

bank.q: Which of the following is a distinctively Indian remedy with no direct counterpart in the other two systems?
bank.e: Continuing mandamus — ongoing judicial supervision of executive compliance — grew out of Indian public interest litigation.
